title: A jealous brother
hookLine: his elder brother Prithi Chand resents him and makes trouble for years

lines: PRITHI CHAND DOES NOT ACCEPT IT.
cards: Who got the bigger room. Who Dad liked more. Some arguments outlive the house they started in, and a holiday dinner turns into careful choices about where people sit.
The Bible tells stories like this too: Cain and Abel, Joseph and his brothers. The Sikh story has one.
Arjan was now the fifth Guru, and his eldest brother, Prithi Chand, the one who intercepted the letters, did not accept it. Tradition says he never did.

teach.h: A RIVAL GURU, A HUNGRY KITCHEN.
teach.b: Prithi Chand set himself up as a rival Guru. Tradition says he gathered his own followers and collected offerings meant for the Guru's kitchen, so that for a while the langar at Amritsar ran short.
He even wrote hymns of his own signed with the name Nanak, as if they were the Gurus' words. Bhai Gurdas, the Sikh poet, gave his followers a sharp name: minas, the deceivers.
Tradition tells darker stories too, of attempts to harm Guru Arjan's young son, Hargobind: a nurse with poison, a snake, a poisoned dish.
Each time, the stories say, the child was spared. So how did Guru Arjan respond?

teach.h: NO ARMY, NO CURSE. HE KEPT WORKING.
teach.b: He didn't raise an army against his brother. He didn't curse him. He kept doing his work: building, singing, serving the community.
And he trusted his son's life to God. The scripture holds hymns of Guru Arjan's full of gratitude for protection.

teach.h: THE HOT WIND CANNOT TOUCH HIM.
teach.b: In one, he says, in paraphrase, that the hot wind cannot touch the one who is under God's shelter. Sikh tradition links some of them to those years.
So the line, pray for the difficult one, doesn't mean pretending it's fine. The offerings really go missing; the child is really in danger. What the Guru refuses is to become like his brother.
He leaves him to God and keeps his own work going: a Guru, and still a brother, across the table from someone who wanted his place.

how: Sikhs remember Prithi Chand's rivalry as a hard chapter in Guru Arjan's life, and read Guru Arjan's hymns of protection and trust in God, some sung in daily prayers, with those years in mind.

games.q: you're Guru Arjan. your elder brother has set up a rival court, diverted offerings and wants you gone. what do you do?
o: gather your followers and confront him.
keep working, and leave him in God's hands.
give him the Guruship to keep the peace.
games.why: Guru Arjan neither fought nor gave in. he went on building and serving, and trusted his family's safety to God.

practice: Bring to mind one difficult relationship in your family, or close to it, without replaying the argument or planning what you'll say next time. Let the person's face be there, and notice what happens in your chest.
If you pray, hold them before God in whatever words you use; if you don't, just wish them one good thing.

wordCard.voice: Prithi Chand. Guru Arjan's eldest brother, who set himself up as a rival Guru for years, and whom the Guru answered with work, not revenge.

carryVoice: Your line: pray for the difficult one. Even through your teeth, even once. Until tomorrow, then.
